rules.title: Reglas de Mitchi
rules.intro: [ES] Everything you need to play, from setup to the end of the game.

overview.heading: Resumen
overview.summary: [ES] Mitchi is a dice game for two or more players, played over a series of rounds. Each round, you roll to avoid being left with the worst hand. The player with the worst hand takes the points in the pot. When the game ends, the player with the fewest points wins.

youNeed.heading: Qué necesitas
youNeed.paper: [ES] A pen and paper to keep score

setup.heading: Preparación
setup.pointLimit: [ES] Agree a point limit. 25 is usual. Choose a lower limit for a shorter game.
setup.whoStarts: [ES] Decide who starts. Everyone rolls one die, and the highest roll starts. If the highest roll is tied, those players roll again. Play goes clockwise.

hands.heading: Manos
hands.intro: [ES] A hand is the two dice you finish your turn with. There are six groups of hands, from best to worst:
hands.allHandsLink: Las 21 manos están incluidas en la <reference>referencia rápida</reference>.

rollLimit.heading: [ES] The starting player sets the roll limit
rollLimit.rolls: [ES] The starting player rolls both dice, up to three times, and can stop after any roll. After each roll, they can:
rollLimit.keepOne: [ES] keep one die and re-roll the other
rollLimit.newChoice: [ES] Each roll is a new choice. Keeping a die on one roll does not mean keeping it on the next. Re-rolling one die still counts as a roll.
rollLimit.setsLimit: [ES] The number of rolls the starting player uses is the <term>roll limit</term> for everyone else that round.
rollLimit.example: [ES] The starting player rolls six-three in two rolls. Everyone else gets up to two rolls.

everyoneElse.heading: [ES] Everyone else
everyoneElse.turn: [ES] Everyone else takes a turn in clockwise order, with the same choices, up to the roll limit. You do not have to use every roll. Stop when you are happy with your hand.
everyoneElse.worstHandSoFar: [ES] You never need the best hand. You only need to beat the <term>worst hand so far</term>: the lowest-ranked hand rolled this round. It changes as players finish their turn, so a later player may have less to beat than an earlier one.
everyoneElse.example1: [ES] Player {a} rolls six-four in one. Player {b} rolls five-one. Player {c} now needs five-two or better, because five-one is the worst hand so far.
everyoneElse.example2: [ES] Player {a} rolls five-four in three. Player {b} rolls six-two in one. That already beats five-four, so Player {b} stops.

scoring.heading: La puntuación de la ronda
scoring.startingPot: [ES] Every round starts with 1 point in <term>the pot</term>.
scoring.mitchis: [ES] The first Mitchi rolled replaces that point with 2 points. Each Mitchi after that adds 2 more, so the pot is 2 points for every Mitchi rolled.
scoring.takeThePot: [ES] At the end of the round, the player with the worst hand <term>takes the pot</term> and adds the points to their score. They start the next round.

tieBreaks.heading: Desempates
tieBreaks.intro: [ES] If two or more players are tied on the worst hand, they play a <term>tie-break</term> to decide who takes the pot.
tieBreaks.rollOnce: [ES] Roll once each. Only the tied players roll, with no re-rolls. Go in the opposite direction to the last round or tie-break, starting with the last player to roll.
tieBreaks.addMitchis: [ES] Add 2 points for each Mitchi rolled in the tie-break.
tieBreaks.worstHandTakes: [ES] The worst hand takes the pot. If players tie again, go back to step 1 with only those players.

example.tied: [ES] Three players tie on the worst hand
example.takesPot: [ES] One player has the worst hand and takes the pot

winning.heading: Ganar la partida
winning.gameEnds: [ES] The game ends when any player reaches the point limit. The player with the fewest points wins.
winning.tiedOnFewest: [ES] If players are tied on the fewest points, they roll once each, and the best hand wins.

reference.title: Referencia rápida
reference.intro: [ES] Everything you need mid-game, on one screen.

ranking.heading: Clasificación de las manos
ranking.intro: [ES] Best at the top, worst at the bottom. Within a group, the higher hand wins. The worst hand in the game is three-one.
ranking.tableCaption: Las manos de Mitchi, clasificadas de mejor a peor

scoring.heading: Puntuación
scoring.intro: [ES] Every round starts with 1 point in the pot. The first Mitchi replaces it with 2 points, and each Mitchi after that adds 2 more. The worst hand takes the pot and starts the next round.

tieBreaks.heading: Desempates
tieBreaks.intro: [ES] Tied players roll once each. The worst hand takes the pot.
tieBreaks.eachMitchi: [ES] Each Mitchi rolled in a tie-break

pointLimit.heading: Límite de puntos
pointLimit.summary: [ES] The game ends when any player reaches the point limit, usually 25. The fewest points wins. If players are tied on the fewest points, they roll once each and the best hand wins.

about.title: Acerca de Mitchi
about.intro: [ES] How I learnt the game, and why the rules are written down here.

origin.heading: [ES] Where it came from
origin.learnt: [ES] I learnt Mitchi from my cousin around 2010, while I was living in Sanlúcar de Barrameda, in Andalucía. After work, between three and six of us would meet at La Gitana, a bar in town, and play on the bar top.
origin.unknown: [ES] I do not know who taught my cousin, or where the name comes from. I have never met anyone who plays it outside his group of friends.

whyItStuck.heading: [ES] Why it stuck
whyItStuck.easy: [ES] It is easy to learn, and two dice fit in a pocket, so you can play almost anywhere. Rounds are fast.
whyItStuck.tactical: [ES] Everyone can see the scores, so it gets tactical. You might try to push the leader into taking points. Or, if someone is close to the point limit and you are not winning, you might play to keep points away from them, so the game does not end before you can catch up.

writtenDown.heading: [ES] Why I wrote it down
writtenDown.reason: [ES] I had not played for years and wanted to teach some friends, but I could not find the rules written down anywhere. So I wrote them down from memory, and checked anything I was not sure of with my cousin. This site is so anyone can learn it.

mitchiSpeak.heading: [ES] Mitchi Speak
mitchiSpeak.names: [ES] The longer a group plays, the more it gives hands its own names. In ours, five-four was {kenwright}, because one friend would so often stop on it after a single roll. Five-three, one hand worse, became {kenwrong}. My cousin added {jc} for double-three. I never found out why.
mitchiSpeak.yourOwn: [ES] None of these change the rules. Every group ends up with its own. Make up yours.

relatedGames.heading: [ES] Related games
relatedGames.intro: [ES] Mitchi is not the only game where a 2 and a 1 is the best hand. While building this site I came across a couple of others, and there are probably more.
relatedGames.mia: [ES] Mia: the dice are rolled in secret under a cup, and players call out their hand. They can bluff.
relatedGames.mexico: [ES] Mexico: players roll to avoid the lowest hand, losing a life each time, until one player is left.
